speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble eating and a swollen belly. Can you tell me if you are vomiting, especially if it looks like you are throwing up what you just ate?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: That sounds painful. Can you tell me if you are passing any stool, and if so, has it ever looked like "currant jelly" (dark red blood mixed with mucus)?

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
No fever, vomiting, or diarrhea, and a normal birth history helps narrow this down. Do the stools look like "currant jelly" (dark red blood mixed with mucus), or is there any blood in the diaper?
Also, please describe the crying: does it become high-pitched and the baby draw their legs up when the belly hurts?
REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception

The absence of "currant jelly" stools and normal birth history makes this less typical, but the worsening distension, decreased feeding, and pain with palpation are concerning. I have requested an abdominal ultrasound to confirm this immediately.
